-moz-float-edge.name: -moz-float-edge
-moz-float-edge.description: The non-standard -moz-float-edge CSS property specifies whether the height and width properties of the element include the margin, border, or padding thickness.

-moz-force-broken-image-icon.name: -moz-force-broken-image-icon
-moz-force-broken-image-icon.description: The -moz-force-broken-image-icon extended CSS property can be used to force the broken image icon to be shown even when a broken image has an alt attribute.

-moz-orient.name: -moz-orient
-moz-orient.description: The -moz-orient CSS property specifies the orientation of the element to which it's applied.

-moz-user-input.name: -moz-user-input
-moz-user-input.description: In Mozilla applications, -moz-user-input determines if an element will accept user input.

-webkit-border-before.name: -webkit-border-before
-webkit-border-before.description: The -webkit-border-before CSS shorthand property sets the individual logical block start border property values in a single place in the style sheet.

-webkit-box-reflect.name: -webkit-box-reflect
-webkit-box-reflect.description: The -webkit-box-reflect CSS property lets you reflect the content of an element in one specific direction.

-webkit-mask-box-image.name: -webkit-mask-box-image
-webkit-mask-box-image.description: The non-standard prefixed -webkit-mask-box-image CSS shorthand property sets the mask image for an element's border box.

-webkit-mask-composite.name: -webkit-mask-composite
-webkit-mask-composite.description: The -webkit-mask-composite property specifies the manner in which multiple mask images applied to the same element are composited with one another. Mask images are composited in the opposite order that they are declared with the "mask-image", "-webkit-mask-image" property.

-webkit-mask-position-x.name: -webkit-mask-position-x
-webkit-mask-position-x.description: The -webkit-mask-position-x CSS property sets the initial horizontal position of a mask image.

-webkit-mask-position-y.name: -webkit-mask-position-y
-webkit-mask-position-y.description: The -webkit-mask-position-y CSS property sets the initial vertical position of a mask image.

-webkit-tap-highlight-color.name: -webkit-tap-highlight-color
-webkit-tap-highlight-color.description: -webkit-tap-highlight-color is a non-standard CSS property that sets the color of the highlight that appears over a link while it's being tapped. The highlighting indicates to the user that their tap is being successfully recognized, and indicates which element they're tapping on.

-webkit-text-fill-color.name: -webkit-text-fill-color
-webkit-text-fill-color.description: The -webkit-text-fill-color CSS property specifies the fill color of characters of text. If this property is not set, the value of the "color" property is used.

-webkit-text-security.name: -webkit-text-security
-webkit-text-security.description: -webkit-text-security is a non-standard CSS property that obfuscates characters in a "form" field (such as "input" or "textarea") by replacing them with a shape. It only affects fields that are not of type=password.

-webkit-text-stroke.name: -webkit-text-stroke
-webkit-text-stroke.description: The -webkit-text-stroke CSS shorthand property specifies the width and color of strokes for text characters.

-webkit-text-stroke-color.name: -webkit-text-stroke-color
-webkit-text-stroke-color.description: The -webkit-text-stroke-color CSS property specifies the stroke color of characters of text. If this property is not set, the value of the "color" property is used.

-webkit-text-stroke-width.name: -webkit-text-stroke-width
-webkit-text-stroke-width.description: The -webkit-text-stroke-width CSS property specifies the width of the stroke for text.

-webkit-touch-callout.name: -webkit-touch-callout
-webkit-touch-callout.description: The -webkit-touch-callout CSS property controls the display of the default callout shown when you touch and hold a touch target.

accent-color.name: accent-color
accent-color.description: The accent-color CSS property sets the "accent" color for user-interface controls generated by some elements.

align-content.name: align-content
align-content.description: The CSS align-content property sets the distribution of space between and around content items along a flexbox's cross axis, or a grid or block-level element's block axis.
align-content.appliesTo: block containers, multicol containers, flex containers, and grid containers

align-items.name: align-items
align-items.description: The CSS align-items property sets the "align-self" value on all direct children as a group. In flexbox, it controls the alignment of items on the "cross axis". In grid layout, it controls the alignment of items on the block axis within their "grid areas".

align-self.name: align-self
align-self.description: The align-self CSS property overrides a grid or flex item's "align-items" value. In grid, it aligns the item inside the "Grid Areas", "grid area". In flexbox, it aligns the item on the "cross axis".
align-self.appliesTo: flex items, grid items, and absolutely-positioned boxes

alignment-baseline.name: alignment-baseline
alignment-baseline.description: The alignment-baseline CSS property specifies the specific baseline used to align the box's text and inline-level contents. Baseline alignment is the relationship among the baselines of multiple alignment subjects within an alignment context. When performing baseline alignment, the alignment-baseline property value specifies which baseline of the box is aligned to the corresponding baseline of its alignment context.
alignment-baseline.appliesTo: inline-level boxes, flex items, grid items, table cells, and SVG text content elements

all.name: all
all.description: The all CSS shorthand property resets all of an element's properties except "unicode-bidi", "direction", and CSS Custom Properties. It can set properties to their initial or inherited values, or to the values specified in another cascade layer or stylesheet origin.
all.syntax: initial | inherit | unset | revert | revert-layer | revert-rule

anchor-name.name: anchor-name
anchor-name.description: The anchor-name CSS property enables defining an element as an anchor element by giving it one or more identifying anchor names. Each name can then be set as the value of a positioned element's "position-anchor" property to associate it with the anchor.
anchor-name.appliesTo: all elements that generate a principal box

anchor-scope.name: anchor-scope
anchor-scope.description: The anchor-scope CSS property can be used to limit the scope in which a positioned element can be associated with anchor elements to a particular subtree.

animation.name: animation
animation.description: The animation CSS shorthand property applies an animation between styles. It is a shorthand for "animation-name", "animation-duration", "animation-timing-function", "animation-delay", "animation-iteration-count", "animation-direction", "animation-fill-mode", "animation-play-state", and "animation-timeline".

animation-composition.name: animation-composition
animation-composition.description: The animation-composition CSS property specifies the "composite operation" to use when multiple animations affect the same property simultaneously.

animation-delay.name: animation-delay
animation-delay.description: The animation-delay CSS property specifies the amount of time to wait from applying the animation to an element before beginning to perform the animation. The animation can start later, immediately from its beginning, or immediately and partway through the animation.

animation-direction.name: animation-direction
animation-direction.description: The animation-direction CSS property sets whether an animation should play forward, backward, or alternate back and forth between playing the sequence forward and backward.

animation-duration.name: animation-duration
animation-duration.description: The animation-duration CSS property sets the length of time that an animation takes to complete one cycle.

animation-fill-mode.name: animation-fill-mode
animation-fill-mode.description: The animation-fill-mode CSS property sets how a CSS animation applies styles to its target before and after its execution.

animation-iteration-count.name: animation-iteration-count
animation-iteration-count.description: The animation-iteration-count CSS property sets the number of times an animation sequence should be played before stopping.

animation-name.name: animation-name
animation-name.description: The animation-name CSS property specifies the names of one or more "@keyframes" at-rules that describe the animation to apply to an element. Multiple @keyframes at-rules are specified as a comma-separated list of names. If the specified name does not match any @keyframes at-rule, no properties are animated.

animation-play-state.name: animation-play-state
animation-play-state.description: The animation-play-state CSS property sets whether an animation is running or paused.

animation-range.name: animation-range
animation-range.description: The animation-range CSS shorthand property is used to set the start and end of an animation's attachment range along its timeline, i.e., where along the timeline an animation will start and end.

animation-range-end.name: animation-range-end
animation-range-end.description: The animation-range-end CSS property sets the point on the timeline where an animation should end.

animation-range-start.name: animation-range-start
animation-range-start.description: The animation-range-start CSS property sets the point on the timeline where an animation should start.

animation-timeline.name: animation-timeline
animation-timeline.description: The animation-timeline CSS property specifies the timeline used to control the progress of a CSS animation.

animation-timing-function.name: animation-timing-function
animation-timing-function.description: The animation-timing-function CSS property sets how an animation progresses through the duration of each cycle.

animation-trigger.name: animation-trigger
animation-trigger.description: The animation-trigger CSS property specifies whether CSS animations declared on an element are triggered animations (or not) and, if so, what their triggers are and how they should behave when the trigger becomes active or inactive. This is used to create scroll-triggered animations.

appearance.name: appearance
appearance.description: The appearance CSS property specifies the rendered appearance of replaced UI widget elements such as form controls. Most commonly, such elements are given native, platform-specific styling based on the operating system's theme, or a primitive appearance with styles that can be overridden using CSS.

aspect-ratio.name: aspect-ratio
aspect-ratio.description: The aspect-ratio CSS property allows you to define the desired width-to-height ratio of an element's box.
aspect-ratio.appliesTo: all elements except inline boxes and internal ruby or table boxes

backdrop-filter.name: backdrop-filter
backdrop-filter.description: The backdrop-filter CSS property lets you apply graphical effects such as blurring or color shifting to the area behind an element. Because it applies to everything behind the element, to see the effect the element or its background needs to be transparent or partially transparent.
backdrop-filter.appliesTo: All elements. In SVG, it applies to container elements without the defs element and all graphics elements

backface-visibility.name: backface-visibility
backface-visibility.description: The backface-visibility CSS property sets whether the back face of an element is visible when turned towards the user.

background.name: background
background.description: The background CSS shorthand property sets all background style properties at once, such as color, image, origin, size, and repeat method.

background-attachment.name: background-attachment
background-attachment.description: The background-attachment CSS property sets whether a background image's position is fixed within the "viewport", or scrolls with its containing block.

background-blend-mode.name: background-blend-mode
background-blend-mode.description: The background-blend-mode CSS property sets how an element's background images should blend with each other and with the element's background color.

background-clip.name: background-clip
background-clip.description: The background-clip CSS property sets whether an element's background extends underneath its border box, padding box, or content box.

background-color.name: background-color
background-color.description: The background-color CSS property sets the background color of an element.

background-image.name: background-image
background-image.description: The background-image CSS property sets one or more background images on an element.

background-origin.name: background-origin
background-origin.description: The background-origin CSS property sets the background's origin: from the border start, inside the border, or inside the padding.

background-position.name: background-position
background-position.description: The background-position CSS property sets the initial position for each background image.

background-position-x.name: background-position-x
background-position-x.description: The background-position-x CSS property sets the initial horizontal position for each background image. The position is relative to the position layer set by "background-origin".

background-position-y.name: background-position-y
background-position-y.description: The background-position-y CSS property sets the initial vertical position for each background image. The position is relative to the position layer set by "background-origin".

background-repeat.name: background-repeat
background-repeat.description: The background-repeat CSS shorthand property sets how background images are repeated. A background image can be repeated along the horizontal and vertical axes, or not repeated at all.

background-repeat-x.name: background-repeat-x
background-repeat-x.description: The background-repeat-x CSS property sets how background images are repeated, or not, along the horizontal axis.

background-repeat-y.name: background-repeat-y
background-repeat-y.description: The background-repeat-y CSS property sets how background images are repeated, or not, along the vertical axis.

background-size.name: background-size
background-size.description: The background-size CSS property sets the size of the element's background image. The image can be left to its natural size, stretched, or constrained to fit the available space.

baseline-shift.name: baseline-shift
baseline-shift.description: The baseline-shift CSS property repositions the dominant-baseline of a text element relative to the dominant-baseline of its parent text content element. The shifted element might be a sub- or superscript. If the property is present, the value overrides the element's "baseline-shift" attribute.
baseline-shift.appliesTo: inline-level boxes and SVG text content elements

baseline-source.name: baseline-source
baseline-source.description: The baseline-source CSS property defines which baseline to use when inline-level boxes have multiple possible baselines, such as multi-line inline blocks or inline flex containers. The values allow for choosing between aligning to the box's first baseline, last baseline, or letting the browser decide automatically based on the box type.
baseline-source.appliesTo: inline-level boxes that establish an independent formatting context

block-size.name: block-size
block-size.description: The block-size CSS property defines the size of an element's block along the block axis. If the "writing-mode" is horizontal, it corresponds to the "height"; if the writing mode is vertical, it corresponds to the "width". A related property is "inline-size", which defines the other dimension of the element.

border.name: border
border.description: The border CSS shorthand property sets an element's border. It sets the values of "border-width", "border-style", and "border-color".
border.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-block.name: border-block
border-block.description: The border-block CSS shorthand property sets the individual logical block border property values in a single place in the style sheet.

border-block-color.name: border-block-color
border-block-color.description: The border-block-color CSS property defines the color of the logical block borders of an element, which maps to a physical border color depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "border-top-color" and "border-bottom-color", or "border-right-color" and "border-left-color" property depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".

border-block-end.name: border-block-end
border-block-end.description: The border-block-end CSS shorthand property sets the individual logical block-end border property values in a single place in the style sheet.
border-block-end.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-block-end-color.name: border-block-end-color
border-block-end-color.description: The border-block-end-color CSS property defines the color of the logical block-end border of an element, which maps to a physical border color depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "border-top-color", "border-right-color", "border-bottom-color", or "border-left-color" property depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".
border-block-end-color.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-block-end-style.name: border-block-end-style
border-block-end-style.description: The border-block-end-style CSS property defines the style of the logical block-end border of an element, which maps to a physical border style depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "border-top-style", "border-right-style", "border-bottom-style", or "border-left-style" property depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".
border-block-end-style.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-block-end-width.name: border-block-end-width
border-block-end-width.description: The border-block-end-width CSS property defines the width of the logical block-end border of an element, which maps to a physical border width depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "border-top-width", "border-right-width", "border-bottom-width", or "border-left-width" property depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".
border-block-end-width.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-block-start.name: border-block-start
border-block-start.description: The border-block-start CSS shorthand property sets the individual logical block-start border property values in a single place in the style sheet.
border-block-start.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-block-start-color.name: border-block-start-color
border-block-start-color.description: The border-block-start-color CSS property defines the color of the logical block-start border of an element, which maps to a physical border color depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "border-top-color", "border-right-color", "border-bottom-color", or "border-left-color" property depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".

border-block-start-width.description: The border-block-start-width CSS property defines the width of the logical block-start border of an element, which maps to a physical border width depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. border-block-style.description: The border-block-style CSS property defines the style of the logical block borders of an element, which maps to a physical border style depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "border-top-style" and "border-bottom-style", or "border-left-style" and "border-right-style" properties depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".

border-block-width.name: border-block-width
border-block-width.description: The border-block-width CSS property defines the width of the logical block borders of an element, which maps to a physical border width depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "border-top-width" and "border-bottom-width", or "border-left-width", and "border-right-width" property depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".

border-bottom.name: border-bottom
border-bottom.description: The border-bottom CSS shorthand property sets an element's bottom border. It sets the values of "border-bottom-width", "border-bottom-style" and "border-bottom-color".
border-bottom.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-bottom-color.name: border-bottom-color
border-bottom-color.description: The border-bottom-color CSS property sets the color of an element's bottom border. It can also be set with the shorthand CSS properties "border-color" or "border-bottom".
border-bottom-color.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-bottom-left-radius.name: border-bottom-left-radius
border-bottom-left-radius.description: The border-bottom-left-radius CSS property rounds the bottom-left corner of an element by specifying the radius (or the radius of the semi-major and semi-minor axes) of the ellipse defining the curvature of the corner.

border-bottom-right-radius.name: border-bottom-right-radius
border-bottom-right-radius.description: The border-bottom-right-radius CSS property rounds the bottom-right corner of an element by specifying the radius (or the radius of the semi-major and semi-minor axes) of the ellipse defining the curvature of the corner.

border-bottom-style.name: border-bottom-style
border-bottom-style.description: The border-bottom-style CSS property sets the line style of an element's bottom "border".
border-bottom-style.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-bottom-width.name: border-bottom-width
border-bottom-width.description: The border-bottom-width CSS property sets the width of the bottom border of an element.
border-bottom-width.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-collapse.name: border-collapse
border-collapse.description: The border-collapse CSS property sets whether cells inside a "table" have shared or separate borders.

border-color.name: border-color
border-color.description: The border-color CSS shorthand property sets the color of an element's border.
border-color.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-end-end-radius.name: border-end-end-radius
border-end-end-radius.description: The border-end-end-radius CSS property defines a logical border radius on an element, which maps to a physical border radius that depends on the element's "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation". This is useful when building styles to work regardless of the text orientation and writing mode.

border-end-start-radius.name: border-end-start-radius
border-end-start-radius.description: The border-end-start-radius CSS property defines a logical border radius on an element, which maps to a physical border radius depending on the element's "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation". This is useful when building styles to work regardless of the text orientation and writing mode.

border-image.name: border-image
border-image.description: The border-image CSS shorthand property draws an image around a given element. It replaces the element's regular border.

border-image-outset.name: border-image-outset
border-image-outset.description: The border-image-outset CSS property sets the distance by which an element's border image is set out from its border box.
border-image-outset.appliesTo: All elements, except internal table elements when border-collapse is collapse

border-image-repeat.name: border-image-repeat
border-image-repeat.description: The border-image-repeat CSS property defines how the images for the sides and the middle part of the border image are scaled and tiled. The middle region can be displayed by using the keyword "fill" in the "border-image-slice" property.
border-image-repeat.appliesTo: All elements, except internal table elements when border-collapse is collapse

border-image-slice.name: border-image-slice
border-image-slice.description: The border-image-slice CSS property divides the image specified by "border-image-source" into regions. These regions form the components of an element's border image.
border-image-slice.appliesTo: All elements, except internal table elements when border-collapse is collapse

border-image-source.name: border-image-source
border-image-source.description: The border-image-source CSS property sets the source image used to create an element's border image.
border-image-source.appliesTo: All elements, except internal table elements when border-collapse is collapse

border-image-width.name: border-image-width
border-image-width.description: The border-image-width CSS property sets the width of an element's border image.
border-image-width.appliesTo: All elements, except internal table elements when border-collapse is collapse

border-inline.name: border-inline
border-inline.description: The border-inline CSS shorthand property sets the individual logical inline border property values in a single place in the style sheet.

border-inline-color.name: border-inline-color
border-inline-color.description: The border-inline-color CSS property defines the color of the logical inline borders of an element, which maps to a physical border color depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "border-top-color" and "border-bottom-color", or "border-right-color" and "border-left-color" property depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".

border-inline-end.name: border-inline-end
border-inline-end.description: The border-inline-end CSS shorthand property sets the individual logical inline-end border property values in a single place in the style sheet.
border-inline-end.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

It corresponds to the "border-top-width" and "border-bottom-width", or "border-left-width", and "border-right-width" property depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".

border-left.name: border-left
border-left.description: The border-left CSS shorthand property sets all the properties of an element's left border.
border-left.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-left-color.name: border-left-color
border-left-color.description: The border-left-color CSS property sets the color of an element's left border. It can also be set with the shorthand CSS properties "border-color" or "border-left".
border-left-color.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-left-style.name: border-left-style
border-left-style.description: The border-left-style CSS property sets the line style of an element's left "border".
border-left-style.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-left-width.name: border-left-width
border-left-width.description: The border-left-width CSS property sets the width of the left border of an element.
border-left-width.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-radius.name: border-radius
border-radius.description: The border-radius CSS shorthand property rounds the corners of an element's outer border edge. You can set a single radius to make circular corners, or two radii to make elliptical corners.

border-right.name: border-right
border-right.description: The border-right CSS shorthand property sets all the properties of an element's right border.
border-right.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-right-color.name: border-right-color
border-right-color.description: The border-right-color CSS property sets the color of an element's right border. It can also be set with the shorthand CSS properties "border-color" or "border-right".
border-right-color.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-right-style.name: border-right-style
border-right-style.description: The border-right-style CSS property sets the line style of an element's right "border".
border-right-style.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-right-width.name: border-right-width
border-right-width.description: The border-right-width CSS property sets the width of the right border of an element.
border-right-width.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-shape.name: border-shape
border-shape.description: The border-shape CSS property defines an element's border shape using "basic-shape" values.

border-spacing.name: border-spacing
border-spacing.description: The border-spacing CSS property sets the distance between the borders of adjacent cells in a "table". This property applies only when "border-collapse" is separate.
border-spacing.appliesTo: table grid boxes when border-collapse is separate

border-start-end-radius.name: border-start-end-radius
border-start-end-radius.description: The border-start-end-radius CSS property defines a logical border radius on an element, which maps to a physical border radius depending on the element's "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation". This is useful when building styles to work regardless of the text orientation and writing mode.

border-start-start-radius.name: border-start-start-radius
border-start-start-radius.description: The border-start-start-radius CSS property defines a logical border radius on an element, which maps to a physical border radius that depends on the element's "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation". This is useful when building styles to work regardless of the text orientation and writing mode.

border-style.name: border-style
border-style.description: The border-style CSS shorthand property sets the line style for all four sides of an element's border.
border-style.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-top.name: border-top
border-top.description: The border-top CSS shorthand property sets all the properties of an element's top border.
border-top.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-top-color.name: border-top-color
border-top-color.description: The border-top-color CSS property sets the color of an element's top border. It can also be set with the shorthand CSS properties "border-color" or "border-top".
border-top-color.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-top-left-radius.name: border-top-left-radius
border-top-left-radius.description: The border-top-left-radius CSS property rounds the top-left corner of an element by specifying the radius (or the radius of the semi-major and semi-minor axes) of the ellipse defining the curvature of the corner.

border-top-right-radius.name: border-top-right-radius
border-top-right-radius.description: The border-top-right-radius CSS property rounds the top-right corner of an element by specifying the radius (or the radius of the semi-major and semi-minor axes) of the ellipse defining the curvature of the corner.

border-top-style.name: border-top-style
border-top-style.description: The border-top-style CSS property sets the line style of an element's top "border".
border-top-style.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-top-width.name: border-top-width
border-top-width.description: The border-top-width CSS property sets the width of the top border of an element.
border-top-width.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

border-width.name: border-width
border-width.description: The border-width CSS shorthand property sets the width of an element's border.
border-width.appliesTo: all elements except ruby base containers and ruby annotation containers

bottom.name: bottom
bottom.description: The bottom CSS property participates in setting the vertical position of a positioned element. This "inset properties", "inset property" has no effect on non-positioned elements.

box-align.name: box-align
box-align.description: > [!WARNING] > This is a property of the original CSS flexible box layout Module draft, and has been replaced by a newer standard.

box-decoration-break.name: box-decoration-break
box-decoration-break.description: The box-decoration-break CSS property specifies how an element's fragments should be rendered when broken across multiple lines, columns, or pages.

box-direction.name: box-direction
box-direction.description: > [!WARNING] > This is a property of the original CSS flexible box layout Module draft, and has been replaced by a newer standard. The -moz-box-direction will only be used for XUL while the previous standard box-direction has been replaced by flex-direction. See flexbox for information about the current standard.

box-flex.name: box-flex
box-flex.description: > [!WARNING] > This is a property for controlling parts of the XUL box model. It does not match either the old CSS flexible box layout Module drafts for box-flex (which were based on this property) or the behavior of -webkit-box-flex (which is based on those drafts). See flexbox for information about the current standard.

box-flex-group.name: box-flex-group
box-flex-group.description: > [!WARNING] > This is a property of the original CSS flexible box layout Module draft. It has been replaced in the specification. See flexbox for information about the current standard.

box-lines.name: box-lines
box-lines.description: > [!WARNING] > This is a property of the original CSS flexible box layout Module draft. It has been replaced in the specification. See flexbox for information about the current standard.

box-ordinal-group.name: box-ordinal-group
box-ordinal-group.description: > [!WARNING] > This is a property of the original CSS flexible box layout Module draft. It has been replaced in the specification. See flexbox for information about the current standard.

box-orient.name: box-orient
box-orient.description: > [!WARNING] > This is a property of the original CSS flexible box layout Module draft, and has been replaced by a newer standard. See flexbox for information about the current standard.

box-pack.name: box-pack
box-pack.description: > [!WARNING] > This is a property of the original CSS flexible box layout Module draft, and has been replaced by a newer standard. See flexbox for information about the current standard.

box-shadow.name: box-shadow
box-shadow.description: The box-shadow CSS property adds shadow effects around an element's frame. You can set multiple effects separated by commas. A box shadow is described by X and Y offsets relative to the element, blur and spread radius, and color.

box-sizing.name: box-sizing
box-sizing.description: The box-sizing CSS property sets how the total width and height of an element is calculated.
box-sizing.appliesTo: all elements that accept width or height

break-after.name: break-after
break-after.description: The break-after CSS property sets how page, column, or region breaks should behave after a generated box. If there is no generated box, the property is ignored.
break-after.syntax: auto | avoid | always | all | avoid-page | page | left | right | recto | verso | avoid-column | column | avoid-region | region
break-after.appliesTo: block-level boxes, grid items, flex items, table row groups, table rows (but see prose)

break-before.name: break-before
break-before.description: The break-before CSS property sets how page, column, or region breaks should behave before a generated box. If there is no generated box, the property is ignored.
break-before.syntax: auto | avoid | always | all | avoid-page | page | left | right | recto | verso | avoid-column | column | avoid-region | region
break-before.appliesTo: block-level boxes, grid items, flex items, table row groups, table rows (but see prose)

break-inside.name: break-inside
break-inside.description: The break-inside CSS property sets how page, column, or region breaks should behave inside a generated box. If there is no generated box, the property is ignored.
break-inside.appliesTo: all elements except inline-level boxes, internal ruby boxes, table column boxes, table column group boxes, absolutely-positioned boxes

caption-side.name: caption-side
caption-side.description: The caption-side CSS property puts the content of a table's "caption" on the specified side. The values are relative to the "writing-mode" of the table.

caret-animation.name: caret-animation
caret-animation.description: The caret-animation CSS property is used to enable or disable the blinking behavior of the insertion caret, the visible marker that appears in editable elements to indicate where the next character will be inserted or deleted.
caret-animation.appliesTo: text or elements that accept text input

caret-color.name: caret-color
caret-color.description: The caret-color CSS property sets the color of the insertion caret, sometimes referred to as the text input cursor. This is the visible marker appearing at the insertion point where the next character typed will be added or where the next character deleted will be removed.
caret-color.appliesTo: text or elements that accept text input

caret-shape.name: caret-shape
caret-shape.description: The caret-shape CSS property sets the shape of the insertion caret, the visible marker that appears in editable elements to indicate where the next character will be inserted or deleted.
caret-shape.appliesTo: text or elements that accept text input

clear.name: clear
clear.description: The clear CSS property sets whether an element must be moved below (cleared) floating elements that precede it. The clear property applies to floating and non-floating elements.

clip.name: clip
clip.description: > [!WARNING] > Authors are encouraged to use the "clip-path" property instead.
clip.appliesTo: Absolutely positioned elements. In SVG, it applies to elements which establish a new viewport, pattern elements and mask elements.

clip-path.name: clip-path
clip-path.description: The clip-path CSS property creates a clipping region that sets what part of an element should be shown. Parts that are inside the region are shown, while those outside are hidden.
clip-path.appliesTo: All elements. In SVG, it applies to container elements excluding the defs element, all graphics elements and the use element

clip-rule.name: clip-rule
clip-rule.description: The clip-rule CSS property determines, when parts of the path overlap other parts, which pixels in a mask's box are inside the clipping shape defined by a clip path and which are outside.

color.name: color
color.description: The color CSS property sets the foreground color value of an element's text and text decorations, and sets the currentColor value. currentColor may be used as an indirect value on other properties and is the default for other color properties, such as "border-color".

color-interpolation.name: color-interpolation
color-interpolation.description: The color-interpolation CSS property is used in SVG to specify which color space to use for "linearGradient" and "radialGradient" SVG elements.
color-interpolation.appliesTo: container elements, graphics elements, gradient elements, ‘use’ and ‘animate’

color-interpolation-filters.name: color-interpolation-filters
color-interpolation-filters.description: The color-interpolation-filters CSS property specifies the color space for imaging operations performed via SVG filter effects. If explicitly declared, the value of the CSS property overrides any value given in the element's "color-interpolation-filters" attribute.

color-scheme.name: color-scheme
color-scheme.description: The color-scheme CSS property allows an element to indicate which color schemes it can comfortably be rendered in. User agents change the following aspects of the UI chrome to match the used color scheme:

column-count.name: column-count
column-count.description: The column-count CSS property breaks an element's content into the specified number of columns.
column-count.appliesTo: block containers except table wrapper boxes

column-fill.name: column-fill
column-fill.description: The column-fill CSS property controls how an element's contents are balanced when broken into columns.

column-gap.name: column-gap
column-gap.description: The column-gap CSS property sets the size of the gap ("Gutters","gutter") between an element's columns in multi-column, flexible box, and grid layouts.
column-gap.appliesTo: multi-column containers, flex containers, grid containers, and grid lanes containers

column-height.name: column-height
column-height.description: The column-height CSS property specifies the height of the columns in a CSS multi-column layout.
column-height.appliesTo: block containers except table wrapper boxes

column-rule.name: column-rule
column-rule.description: The column-rule CSS shorthand property sets the width, style, and color of the lines drawn between columns in multi-column grid, flex, and multi-col layouts.

column-rule-break.name: column-rule-break
column-rule-break.description: The column-rule-break CSS property sets the behavior for breaking column rules into segments wherever column rules intersect row gaps.
column-rule-break.appliesTo: grid containers, flex containers, multicol containers, and grid lanes containers

column-rule-color.name: column-rule-color
column-rule-color.description: The column-rule-color CSS property defines the colors of the lines drawn between columns in multi-column grid, flex, and multi-col layouts.
column-rule-color.appliesTo: grid containers, flex containers, multicol containers, and grid lanes containers

column-rule-inset.name: column-rule-inset
column-rule-inset.appliesTo: Same as column-rule-inset-cap, column-rule-inset-junction, row-rule-inset-cap, and row-rule-inset-junction

column-rule-inset-cap.name: column-rule-inset-cap
column-rule-inset-cap.description: The column-rule-inset-cap shorthand CSS property can be used to offset the column rule segment cap endpoints at the container's start and end edges, and endpoints where the segments don't intersect other row or column segments.
column-rule-inset-cap.appliesTo: Same as column-rule-inset-cap-start, column-rule-inset-cap-end, column-rule-inset-junction-start, column-rule-inset-junction-end, row-rule-inset-cap-start, row-rule-inset-cap-end, row-rule-inset-junction-start, and row-rule-inset-junction-end

column-rule-inset-cap-end.name: column-rule-inset-cap-end
column-rule-inset-cap-end.description: The column-rule-inset-cap-end CSS property can be used to offset the bottom of column rule segment cap endpoints at the container's end edge, and cap endpoints where no rule segments intersect.
column-rule-inset-cap-end.appliesTo: grid containers, flex containers, multicol containers, and grid lanes containers

column-rule-inset-cap-start.name: column-rule-inset-cap-start
column-rule-inset-cap-start.description: The column-rule-inset-cap-start CSS property can be used to offset the top of column rule segment cap endpoints at the container's start edge, and cap endpoints where no rule segments intersect.
column-rule-inset-cap-start.appliesTo: grid containers, flex containers, multicol containers, and grid lanes containers

column-rule-inset-end.name: column-rule-inset-end
column-rule-inset-end.appliesTo: Same as column-rule-inset-cap-start, column-rule-inset-junction-start, column-rule-inset-cap-end, column-rule-inset-junction-end, row-rule-inset-cap-start, row-rule-inset-junction-start, row-rule-inset-cap-end, and row-rule-inset-junction-end

column-rule-inset-junction.name: column-rule-inset-junction
column-rule-inset-junction.description: The column-rule-inset-junction CSS shorthand property can be used to offset both the top and bottom endpoints of column rule segments that are junction endpoints; that is, endpoints at gap junctions where rule segments intersect.
column-rule-inset-junction.appliesTo: Same as column-rule-inset-cap-start, column-rule-inset-cap-end, column-rule-inset-junction-start, column-rule-inset-junction-end, row-rule-inset-cap-start, row-rule-inset-cap-end, row-rule-inset-junction-start, and row-rule-inset-junction-end

column-rule-inset-junction-end.name: column-rule-inset-junction-end
column-rule-inset-junction-end.description: The column-rule-inset-junction-end CSS property can be used to offset the bottom endpoints of column rule segments that are junction endpoints; that is, endpoints at gap junctions where rule segments intersect.
column-rule-inset-junction-end.appliesTo: grid containers, flex containers, multicol containers, and grid lanes containers

column-rule-inset-junction-start.name: column-rule-inset-junction-start
column-rule-inset-junction-start.description: The column-rule-inset-junction-start CSS property can be used to offset the top endpoints of column rule segments that are junction endpoints; that is, endpoints at gap junctions where rule segments intersect.
column-rule-inset-junction-start.appliesTo: grid containers, flex containers, multicol containers, and grid lanes containers

column-rule-inset-start.name: column-rule-inset-start
column-rule-inset-start.appliesTo: Same as column-rule-inset-cap-start, column-rule-inset-junction-start, column-rule-inset-cap-end, column-rule-inset-junction-end, row-rule-inset-cap-start, row-rule-inset-junction-start, row-rule-inset-cap-end, and row-rule-inset-junction-end

column-rule-style.name: column-rule-style
column-rule-style.description: The column-rule-style CSS property defines the line style of the lines drawn between columns in multi-column grid, flex, and multi-col layouts.
column-rule-style.appliesTo: grid containers, flex containers, multicol containers, and grid lanes containers

column-rule-visibility-items.name: column-rule-visibility-items
column-rule-visibility-items.description: The column-rule-visibility-items CSS property defines whether a column-rule segment is painted in gaps adjacent to empty areas.

column-rule-width.name: column-rule-width
column-rule-width.description: The column-rule-width CSS property defines the widths of the lines drawn between columns in multi-column grid, flex, and multi-col layouts.
column-rule-width.appliesTo: grid containers, flex containers, multicol containers, and grid lanes containers

column-span.name: column-span
column-span.description: The column-span CSS property makes it possible for an element to span across all columns when its value is set to all.

column-width.name: column-width
column-width.description: The column-width CSS property sets the ideal column width in a multi-column layout.
column-width.appliesTo: block containers except table wrapper boxes

column-wrap.name: column-wrap
column-wrap.description: The column-wrap CSS property specifies the wrapping behavior of overflow columns in a CSS multi-column layout.

columns.name: columns
columns.description: The columns CSS shorthand property sets the maximum number of columns to use when drawing an element's contents, along with the minimum width and maximum height of the element's columns.

contain.name: contain
contain.description: The contain CSS property indicates that an element and its contents are, as much as possible, independent from the rest of the document tree. Containment enables isolating a subsection of the DOM, providing performance benefits by limiting calculations of layout, style, paint, size, or any combination to a DOM subtree rather than the entire page. Containment can also be used to scope CSS counters and quotes.
contain.syntax: none | strict | content | [ [size | inline-size] || layout || style || paint ]

contain-intrinsic-block-size.name: contain-intrinsic-block-size
contain-intrinsic-block-size.description: The contain-intrinsic-block-size CSS logical property defines the block size of an element that a browser can use for layout when the element is subject to size containment.

contain-intrinsic-height.name: contain-intrinsic-height
contain-intrinsic-height.description: The contain-intrinsic-height CSS property sets the height of an element that a browser can use for layout when the element is subject to size containment.

contain-intrinsic-inline-size.name: contain-intrinsic-inline-size
contain-intrinsic-inline-size.description: The contain-intrinsic-inline-size CSS logical property defines the inline-size of an element that a browser can use for layout when the element is subject to size containment.

contain-intrinsic-size.name: contain-intrinsic-size
contain-intrinsic-size.description: The contain-intrinsic-size CSS shorthand property sets the size of an element that a browser will use for layout when the element is subject to size containment.

contain-intrinsic-width.name: contain-intrinsic-width
contain-intrinsic-width.description: The contain-intrinsic-width CSS property sets the width of an element that a browser will use for layout when the element is subject to size containment.

container.name: container
container.description: The container shorthand CSS property establishes the element as a query container and specifies the name and type of the containment context used in a container query.

container-name.name: container-name
container-name.description: The container-name CSS property specifies a list of query container names used by the @container at-rule in a container query.

container-type.name: container-type
container-type.description: The container-type CSS property specifies the type of container context used in a container query.

content.name: content
content.description: The content CSS property replaces content with a generated value. It can be used to define what is rendered inside an element or pseudo-element. For elements, the content property specifies whether the element renders normally (normal or none) or is replaced with an image (and associated "alt" text). For pseudo-elements and margin boxes, content defines the content as images, text, both, or none, which determines whether the element renders at all.
content.appliesTo: all elements, tree-abiding pseudo-elements, and page margin boxes

content-visibility.name: content-visibility
content-visibility.description: The content-visibility CSS property controls whether or not an element renders its contents at all, along with forcing a strong set of containments, allowing user agents to potentially omit large swathes of layout and rendering work until it becomes needed. It enables the user agent to skip an element's rendering work (including layout and painting) until it is needed — which makes the initial page load much faster.
content-visibility.appliesTo: elements for which size containment can apply

corner-block-end-shape.name: corner-block-end-shape
corner-block-end-shape.description: The corner-block-end-shape CSS property specifies the shape of both the corners on a box's block-end edge, within their "border-radius" area.

corner-block-start-shape.name: corner-block-start-shape
corner-block-start-shape.description: The corner-block-start-shape CSS property specifies the shape of both the corners on a box's block-start edge, within their "border-radius" area.

corner-bottom-left-shape.name: corner-bottom-left-shape
corner-bottom-left-shape.description: The corner-bottom-left-shape CSS property specifies the shape of a box's bottom-left corner, within its "border-radius" area.
corner-bottom-left-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-bottom-right-shape.name: corner-bottom-right-shape
corner-bottom-right-shape.description: The corner-bottom-right-shape CSS property specifies the shape of a box's bottom-right corner, within its "border-radius" area.
corner-bottom-right-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-bottom-shape.name: corner-bottom-shape
corner-bottom-shape.description: The corner-bottom-shape CSS property specifies the shape of both the corners on a box's bottom edge, within their "border-radius" area.

corner-end-end-shape.name: corner-end-end-shape
corner-end-end-shape.description: The corner-end-end-shape CSS property specifies the shape of a box's block-end and inline-end corner, within its "border-radius" area.
corner-end-end-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-end-start-shape.name: corner-end-start-shape
corner-end-start-shape.description: The corner-end-start-shape CSS property specifies the shape of a box's block-end and inline-start corner, within its "border-radius" area.
corner-end-start-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-inline-end-shape.name: corner-inline-end-shape
corner-inline-end-shape.description: The corner-inline-end-shape CSS property specifies the shape of both the corners on a box's inline-end edge, within their "border-radius" area.

corner-inline-start-shape.name: corner-inline-start-shape
corner-inline-start-shape.description: The corner-inline-start-shape CSS property specifies the shape of both the corners on a box's inline-start edge, within their "border-radius" area.

corner-left-shape.name: corner-left-shape
corner-left-shape.description: The corner-left-shape CSS property specifies the shape of both the corners on a box's left-hand edge, within their "border-radius" area.

corner-right-shape.name: corner-right-shape
corner-right-shape.description: The corner-right-shape CSS property specifies the shape of both the corners on a box's right-hand edge, within their "border-radius" area.

corner-shape.name: corner-shape
corner-shape.description: The corner-shape CSS shorthand property specifies the shape of a box's corners, within the area specified by its "border-radius" property value.
corner-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-start-end-shape.name: corner-start-end-shape
corner-start-end-shape.description: The corner-start-end-shape CSS property specifies the shape of a box's block-start and inline-end corner, within its "border-radius" area.
corner-start-end-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-start-start-shape.name: corner-start-start-shape
corner-start-start-shape.description: The corner-start-start-shape CSS property specifies the shape of a box's block-start and inline-start corner, within its "border-radius" area.
corner-start-start-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-top-left-shape.name: corner-top-left-shape
corner-top-left-shape.description: The corner-top-left-shape CSS property specifies the shape of a box's top-left corner, within its "border-radius" area.
corner-top-left-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-top-right-shape.name: corner-top-right-shape
corner-top-right-shape.description: The corner-top-right-shape CSS property specifies the shape of a box's top-right corner, within its "border-radius" area.
corner-top-right-shape.appliesTo: all elements where border-radius can apply

corner-top-shape.name: corner-top-shape
corner-top-shape.description: The corner-top-shape CSS property specifies the shape of both the corners on a box's top edge, within their "border-radius" area.

counter-increment.name: counter-increment
counter-increment.description: The counter-increment CSS property can be used to increase or decrease the value of the named CSS counters by the specified values, or to prevent all counters or an individual counter's value from being changed.

counter-reset.name: counter-reset
counter-reset.description: The counter-reset CSS property creates named CSS counters and initializes their values. It can create both regular and reversed counters.

counter-set.name: counter-set
counter-set.description: The counter-set CSS property sets CSS counters on the element to the given values.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: The cursor CSS property sets the mouse cursor, if any, to show when the mouse pointer is over an element.

cx.name: cx
cx.description: The cx CSS property defines the x-axis center point of an SVG "circle" or "ellipse" element. If present, it overrides the element's "cx" attribute.

cy.name: cy
cy.description: The cy CSS property defines the y-axis center point of an SVG "circle" or "ellipse" elements. If present, it overrides the element's "cy" attribute.

d.name: d
d.description: The d CSS property defines a path to be drawn by the SVG "path" element. If present, it overrides the element's "d" attribute.

direction.name: direction
direction.description: > [!WARNING] > Where possible, authors are encouraged to avoid using the direction CSS property and use the HTML dir global attribute instead.

display.name: display
display.description: The display CSS property sets whether an element is treated as a block or inline box and the layout used for its children, such as flow layout, grid or flex.

dominant-baseline.name: dominant-baseline
dominant-baseline.description: The dominant-baseline CSS property specifies the specific baseline used to align the box's text and inline-level contents. It also indicates the default alignment baseline of any boxes participating in baseline alignment in the box's alignment context. If present, it overrides the shape's "dominant-baseline" attribute.
dominant-baseline.appliesTo: block containers, inline boxes, table rows, grid containers, flex containers, and SVG text content elements

dynamic-range-limit.name: dynamic-range-limit
dynamic-range-limit.description: The dynamic-range-limit CSS property specifies the maximum luminance allowed for High Dynamic Range (HDR) content.

empty-cells.name: empty-cells
empty-cells.description: The empty-cells CSS property sets whether borders and backgrounds appear around "table" cells that have no visible content.

field-sizing.name: field-sizing
field-sizing.description: The field-sizing CSS property enables you to control the sizing behavior of elements that are given a default preferred size, such as form control elements. This property enables you to override the default sizing behavior, allowing form controls to adjust in size to fit their contents.

fill.name: fill
fill.description: The fill CSS property defines how SVG text content and the interior canvas of SVG shapes are filled or painted. If present, it overrides the element's "fill" attribute.

fill-opacity.name: fill-opacity
fill-opacity.description: The fill-opacity CSS property defines the opacity of the painting operation (color, gradient, pattern, etc.) applied to SVG shapes or text content elements to fill the element. The property defines the opacity of the element's fill only; it does not affect the stroke. If present, it overrides the element's "fill-opacity" attribute.

fill-rule.name: fill-rule
fill-rule.description: The fill-rule CSS property defines the rule used to determine which parts of the SVG shape's canvas are included inside a shape to be filled. If present, it overrides the element's "fill-rule" attribute.

filter.name: filter
filter.description: The filter CSS property applies graphical effects like blur or color shift to an element. Filters are commonly used to adjust the rendering of images, backgrounds, and borders.
filter.appliesTo: All elements. In SVG, it applies to container elements without the defs element, all graphics elements and the use element.

flex.name: flex
flex.description: The flex CSS shorthand property sets how a "flex item" will grow or shrink to fit the space available in its flex container.

flex-basis.name: flex-basis
flex-basis.description: The flex-basis CSS property sets the initial main size of a "flex item". It sets the size of the content box unless otherwise set with "box-sizing".

flex-direction.name: flex-direction
flex-direction.description: The flex-direction CSS property sets how flex items are placed in the flex container defining the main axis and the direction (normal or reversed).

flex-flow.name: flex-flow
flex-flow.description: The flex-flow CSS shorthand property specifies the direction of a flex container, as well as its wrapping behavior.

flex-grow.name: flex-grow
flex-grow.description: The flex-grow CSS property sets the flex grow factor, which specifies how much of the flex container's positive free space, if any, should be assigned to the flex item's main size.

flex-line-count.name: flex-line-count
flex-line-count.description: The flex-line-count CSS property sets the minimum number of flex lines that flex items will be balanced over in cases where a flex container's "flex-wrap" or "flex-flow" property includes the balance keyword.

flex-shrink.name: flex-shrink
flex-shrink.description: The flex-shrink CSS property sets the flex shrink factor of a flex item. If the size of all flex items is larger than the flex container, the flex items can shrink to fit according to their flex-shrink value. Each flex line's negative free space is distributed between the line's flex items that have a flex-shrink value greater than 0.

flex-wrap.name: flex-wrap
flex-wrap.description: The flex-wrap CSS property sets whether flex items are forced onto one line or can wrap onto multiple lines. If wrapping is allowed, it sets the direction that lines are stacked.

float.name: float
float.description: The float CSS property places an element on the left or right side of its container, allowing text and inline elements to wrap around it. The element is removed from the normal flow of the page, though still remaining a part of the flow (in contrast to absolute positioning).

flood-color.name: flood-color
flood-color.description: The flood-color CSS property defines the color of the current filter primitive subregion in "feFlood" and "feDropShadow" elements within a "filter". If present, it overrides the element's "flood-color" attribute.

flood-opacity.name: flood-opacity
flood-opacity.description: The flood-opacity CSS property defines the opacity of the current filter primitive subregion in "feFlood" and "feDropShadow" elements within a "filter". If present, it overrides the element's "flood-opacity" attribute.

font.name: font
font.description: The font CSS shorthand property sets all the different properties of an element's font. Alternatively, it sets an element's font to a system font.

font-family.name: font-family
font-family.description: The font-family CSS property specifies a prioritized list of one or more font family names and/or generic family names for the selected element.

font-feature-settings.name: font-feature-settings
font-feature-settings.description: The font-feature-settings CSS property controls advanced typographic features in OpenType fonts.

font-kerning.name: font-kerning
font-kerning.description: The font-kerning CSS property sets the use of the kerning information stored in a font.

font-language-override.name: font-language-override
font-language-override.description: The font-language-override CSS property controls the use of language-specific glyphs in a typeface.

font-optical-sizing.name: font-optical-sizing
font-optical-sizing.description: The font-optical-sizing CSS property sets whether text rendering is optimized for viewing at different sizes.

font-palette.name: font-palette
font-palette.description: The font-palette CSS property allows specifying one of the many palettes contained in a color font that a user agent may use for the font. Users can also override the values in a palette or create a new palette by using the "@font-palette-values" at-rule.

font-size.name: font-size
font-size.description: The font-size CSS property sets the size of the font. Changing the font size also updates the sizes of the font size-relative "<length>" units, such as em, ex, and so forth.

font-size-adjust.name: font-size-adjust
font-size-adjust.description: The font-size-adjust CSS property adjusts the size of a font to match a chosen font metric, such as the height of lowercase letters, to a specified proportion of the "font-size". This property is intended for adjusting fallback fonts to have similar metrics as the first-choice font.
font-size-adjust.syntax: none | [ ex-height | cap-height | ch-width | ic-width | ic-height ]? [ from-font | <number [0,∞]> ]

font-smooth.name: font-smooth
font-smooth.description: The font-smooth CSS property controls the application of anti-aliasing when fonts are rendered.

font-stretch.name: font-stretch
font-stretch.description: > [!NOTE] > The font-stretch property was renamed to "font-width" in the CSS Fonts specification. To preserve compatibility, the specification retains font-stretch as a legacy alias for the font-width property.

font-style.name: font-style
font-style.description: The font-style CSS property sets whether a font should be styled with a normal, italic, or oblique face from its "font-family".

font-synthesis.name: font-synthesis
font-synthesis.description: The font-synthesis CSS shorthand property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize the bold, italic, small-caps, and/or subscript and superscript typefaces when they are missing in the specified font-family.

font-synthesis-position.name: font-synthesis-position
font-synthesis-position.description: The font-synthesis-position CSS property lets you specify whether or not a browser may synthesize the subscript and superscript "position" typefaces when they are missing in a font family, while using "font-variant-position" to set the positions.

font-synthesis-small-caps.name: font-synthesis-small-caps
font-synthesis-small-caps.description: The font-synthesis-small-caps CSS property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize small-caps typeface when it is missing in a font family. Small-caps glyphs typically use the form of uppercase letters but are reduced to the size of lowercase letters.

font-synthesis-style.name: font-synthesis-style
font-synthesis-style.description: The font-synthesis-style CSS property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize the oblique typeface when it is missing in a font family.

font-synthesis-weight.name: font-synthesis-weight
font-synthesis-weight.description: The font-synthesis-weight CSS property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize the bold typeface when it is missing in a font family.

font-variant.name: font-variant
font-variant.description: The font-variant CSS shorthand property allows you to set all the font variants for a font.
font-variant.syntax: normal | none | [ [ <common-lig-values> || <discretionary-lig-values> || <historical-lig-values> || <contextual-alt-values> ] || [ small-caps | all-small-caps | petite-caps | all-petite-caps | unicase | titling-caps ] || [ stylistic(<font-feature-value-name>) || historical-forms || styleset(<font-feature-value-name>#) || character-variant(<font-feature-value-name>#) || swash(<font-feature-value-name>) || ornaments(<font-feature-value-name>) || annotation(<font-feature-value-name>) ] || [ <numeric-figure-values> || <numeric-spacing-values> || <numeric-fraction-values> || ordinal || slashed-zero ] || [ <east-asian-variant-values> || <east-asian-width-values> || ruby ] || [ sub | super ] || [ text | emoji | unicode ] ]

font-variant-alternates.name: font-variant-alternates
font-variant-alternates.description: The font-variant-alternates CSS property controls the usage of alternate glyphs. These alternate glyphs may be referenced by alternative names defined in "@font-feature-values".
font-variant-alternates.syntax: normal | [ stylistic(<font-feature-value-name>) || historical-forms || styleset(<font-feature-value-name>#) || character-variant(<font-feature-value-name>#) || swash(<font-feature-value-name>) || ornaments(<font-feature-value-name>) || annotation(<font-feature-value-name>) ]

font-variant-caps.name: font-variant-caps
font-variant-caps.description: The font-variant-caps CSS property controls the use of alternate glyphs used for small or petite capitals or for titling.
font-variant-caps.syntax: normal | small-caps | all-small-caps | petite-caps | all-petite-caps | unicase | titling-caps

font-variant-east-asian.name: font-variant-east-asian
font-variant-east-asian.description: The font-variant-east-asian CSS property controls the use of alternate glyphs for East Asian scripts, like Japanese and Chinese.

font-variant-emoji.name: font-variant-emoji
font-variant-emoji.description: The font-variant-emoji CSS property specifies the default presentation style for displaying emojis.

font-variant-ligatures.name: font-variant-ligatures
font-variant-ligatures.description: The font-variant-ligatures CSS property controls which "ligature", "ligatures" and contextual forms are used in the textual content of the elements it applies to. This leads to more harmonized forms in the resulting text.

font-variant-numeric.name: font-variant-numeric
font-variant-numeric.description: The font-variant-numeric CSS property controls the usage of alternate glyphs for numbers, fractions, and ordinal markers.

font-variant-position.name: font-variant-position
font-variant-position.description: The font-variant-position CSS property controls the use of alternate, smaller glyphs that are positioned as superscript or subscript.

font-variation-settings.name: font-variation-settings
font-variation-settings.description: The font-variation-settings CSS property provides low-level control over variable font characteristics by letting you specify the four letter axis names of the characteristics you want to vary along with their values.

font-weight.name: font-weight
font-weight.description: The font-weight CSS property sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. The weights available depend on the "font-family" that is currently set.

font-width.name: font-width
font-width.description: > [!NOTE] > The font-width property is the modern replacement for "font-stretch", which is a legacy alias. While font-width is the specification's preferred name, font-stretch currently has broader browser support. Check the fallback example and browser compatibility table for details.
font-width.syntax: normal | <percentage [0,∞]> | ultra-condensed | extra-condensed | condensed | semi-condensed | semi-expanded | expanded | extra-expanded | ultra-expanded

forced-color-adjust.name: forced-color-adjust
forced-color-adjust.description: The forced-color-adjust CSS property allows authors to opt certain elements out of forced colors mode. This then restores the control of those values to CSS.

frame-sizing.name: frame-sizing
frame-sizing.description: The frame-sizing CSS property can be used to set an "iframe" element's horizontal or vertical size to equal the layout size of its embedded document in the same dimension, but only if the embedded document has opted in to sharing its size information.
frame-sizing.appliesTo: replaced elements (but see below for details)

gap.name: gap
gap.description: The gap CSS shorthand property sets the gaps (also called "gutters") between rows and columns on multi-column, flex, and grid containers.
gap.appliesTo: multi-column containers, flex containers, grid containers, and grid lanes containers

grid.name: grid
grid.description: The grid CSS shorthand property sets all of the explicit and implicit grid properties in a single declaration.

grid-area.name: grid-area
grid-area.description: The grid-area CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a "grid", "grid" by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the edges of its "grid areas", "grid area".
grid-area.appliesTo: grid items and absolutely-positioned boxes whose containing block is a grid container

grid-auto-columns.name: grid-auto-columns
grid-auto-columns.description: The grid-auto-columns CSS property specifies the size of an implicitly-created grid column "grid tracks", "track" or pattern of tracks.

grid-auto-flow.name: grid-auto-flow
grid-auto-flow.description: The grid-auto-flow CSS property controls how the auto-placement algorithm works, specifying exactly how auto-placed items get flowed into the grid.

grid-auto-rows.name: grid-auto-rows
grid-auto-rows.description: The grid-auto-rows CSS property specifies the size of an implicitly-created grid row "grid tracks", "track" or pattern of tracks.

grid-column.name: grid-column
grid-column.description: The grid-column CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a "grid column" by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-start and inline-end edge of its "grid areas", "grid area".
grid-column.appliesTo: grid items and absolutely-positioned boxes whose containing block is a grid container

grid-column-end.name: grid-column-end
grid-column-end.description: The grid-column-end CSS property specifies a grid item's end position within the grid column by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the block-end edge of its "grid areas", "grid area".
grid-column-end.appliesTo: grid items and absolutely-positioned boxes whose containing block is a grid container

grid-column-start.name: grid-column-start
grid-column-start.description: The grid-column-start CSS property specifies a grid item's start position within the grid column by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement. This start position defines the block-start edge of the "grid areas", "grid area".
grid-column-start.appliesTo: grid items and absolutely-positioned boxes whose containing block is a grid container

grid-row.name: grid-row
grid-row.description: The grid-row CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a "grid row" by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-start and inline-end edge of its "grid areas", "grid area".
grid-row.appliesTo: grid items and absolutely-positioned boxes whose containing block is a grid container

grid-row-end.name: grid-row-end
grid-row-end.description: The grid-row-end CSS property specifies a grid item's end position within the grid row by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-end edge of its "grid areas", "grid area".
grid-row-end.appliesTo: grid items and absolutely-positioned boxes whose containing block is a grid container

grid-row-start.name: grid-row-start
grid-row-start.description: The grid-row-start CSS property specifies a grid item's start position within the grid row by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-start edge of its "grid areas", "grid area".
grid-row-start.appliesTo: grid items and absolutely-positioned boxes whose containing block is a grid container

grid-template.name: grid-template
grid-template.description: The grid-template CSS shorthand property specifies the "grid column", "grid columns", "gridrow", "grid rows", and "grid areas", "grid areas".

grid-template-areas.name: grid-template-areas
grid-template-areas.description: The grid-template-areas CSS property specifies named "grid areas", establishing the cells in the grid and assigning them names.

grid-template-columns.name: grid-template-columns
grid-template-columns.description: The grid-template-columns CSS property defines the line names and track sizing functions of the "grid column", "grid columns".

grid-template-rows.name: grid-template-rows
grid-template-rows.description: The grid-template-rows CSS property defines the line names and track sizing functions of the "gridrow", "grid rows".

hanging-punctuation.name: hanging-punctuation
hanging-punctuation.description: The hanging-punctuation CSS property specifies whether a punctuation mark should hang at the start or end of a line of text. Hanging punctuation may be placed outside the line box.

height.name: height
height.description: The height CSS property specifies the height of an element. By default, the property defines the height of the content area. If "box-sizing" is set to border-box, however, it instead determines the height of the border area.

hyphenate-character.name: hyphenate-character
hyphenate-character.description: The hyphenate-character CSS property sets the character (or string) used at the end of a line before a hyphenation break.

hyphenate-limit-chars.name: hyphenate-limit-chars
hyphenate-limit-chars.description: The hyphenate-limit-chars CSS property specifies the minimum word length to allow hyphenation of words as well as the minimum number of characters before and after the hyphen.

hyphens.name: hyphens
hyphens.description: The hyphens CSS property specifies how words should be hyphenated when text wraps across multiple lines.

image-orientation.name: image-orientation
image-orientation.description: The image-orientation CSS property specifies a layout-independent correction to the orientation of an image.

image-rendering.name: image-rendering
image-rendering.description: The image-rendering CSS property sets an image scaling algorithm. The property applies to an element itself, to any images set in its other properties, and to its descendants.

initial-letter.name: initial-letter
initial-letter.description: The initial-letter CSS property sets the size and sink for dropped, raised, and sunken initial letters. This property applies to "::first-letter" pseudo-elements and inline-level first children of block containers.
initial-letter.appliesTo: certain inline-level boxes and ::first-letter and inside ::marker boxes (see prose)

inline-size.name: inline-size
inline-size.description: The inline-size CSS property defines the size of an element's block along the inline axis. If the "writing-mode" is horizontal, it corresponds to the "width"; if the writing mode is vertical, it corresponds to the "height". A related property is "block-size", which defines the other dimension of the element.

inset.name: inset
inset.description: The inset CSS shorthand property corresponds to the "top", "right", "bottom", and/or "left" properties. It has the same multi-value syntax of the "margin" shorthand.

inset-block.name: inset-block
inset-block.description: The inset-block CSS shorthand property defines the logical block start and end offsets of an element, which maps to physical offsets depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the "top" and "bottom", or "right" and "left" properties depending on the values defined for "writing-mode", "direction", and "text-orientation".
