top.description: The top CSS property sets the vertical position of a positioned element. This "inset properties", "inset property" has no effect on non-positioned elements.

touch-action.name: touch-action
touch-action.description: The touch-action CSS property sets how an element's region can be manipulated by a touchscreen user (for example, by zooming features built into the browser).
touch-action.syntax: auto | none | [ [ pan-x | pan-left | pan-right ] || [ pan-y | pan-up | pan-down ] || pinch-zoom ] | manipulation
touch-action.appliesTo: all elements except: non-replaced inline elements, table rows, row groups, table columns, and column groups.

transform.name: transform
transform.description: The transform CSS property lets you rotate, scale, skew, or translate an element. It modifies the coordinate space of the CSS visual formatting model.

transform-box.name: transform-box
transform-box.description: The transform-box CSS property defines the layout box to which the "transform", individual transform properties "translate", "scale", and "rotate", and "transform-origin" properties relate.

transform-origin.name: transform-origin
transform-origin.description: The transform-origin CSS property sets the origin for an element's transformations.
transform-origin.syntax: [ left | center | right | top | bottom | <length-percentage> ] | [ left | center | right | <length-percentage> ] [ top | center | bottom | <length-percentage> ] <length>? | [ [ center | left | right ] && [ center | top | bottom ] ] <length>?

transform-style.name: transform-style
transform-style.description: The transform-style CSS property sets whether children of an element are positioned in the 3D space or are flattened in the plane of the element.

transition.name: transition
transition.description: The transition CSS shorthand property for "transition-property", "transition-duration", "transition-timing-function", "transition-delay", and "transition-behavior".

transition-behavior.name: transition-behavior
transition-behavior.description: The transition-behavior CSS property specifies whether transitions will be started for properties whose animation behavior is discrete.

transition-delay.name: transition-delay
transition-delay.description: The transition-delay CSS property specifies the duration to wait before starting a property's transition effect when its value changes.

transition-duration.name: transition-duration
transition-duration.description: The transition-duration CSS property sets the length of time a transition animation should take to complete. By default, the value is 0s, meaning that no animation will occur.

transition-property.name: transition-property
transition-property.description: The transition-property CSS property sets the CSS properties to which a transition effect should be applied.

transition-timing-function.name: transition-timing-function
transition-timing-function.description: The transition-timing-function CSS property sets how intermediate values are calculated for CSS properties being affected by a transition effect.

translate.name: translate
translate.description: The translate CSS property allows you to specify translation transforms individually and independently of the "transform" property. This maps better to typical user interface usage, and saves having to remember the exact order of transform functions to specify in the transform value.

trigger-scope.name: trigger-scope
trigger-scope.description: The trigger-scope CSS property can be used to limit the scope of a scroll-triggered animation trigger name to a document subtree.

unicode-bidi.name: unicode-bidi
unicode-bidi.description: The unicode-bidi CSS property, together with the "direction" property, determines how bidirectional text in a document is handled. For example, if a block of content contains both left-to-right and right-to-left text, the user-agent uses a complex Unicode algorithm to decide how to display the text. The unicode-bidi property overrides this algorithm and allows the developer to control the text embedding.
unicode-bidi.syntax: normal | embed | isolate | bidi-override | isolate-override | plaintext

user-modify.name: user-modify
user-modify.description: The user-modify property has no effect in Firefox. It was originally planned to determine whether or not the content of an element can be edited by a user.

user-select.name: user-select
user-select.description: The user-select CSS property controls whether the user can select text. This doesn't have any effect on content loaded as part of a browser's user interface (its "Chrome", "chrome"), except in textboxes.
user-select.appliesTo: all elements, and optionally to the ::before and ::after pseudo-elements

vector-effect.name: vector-effect
vector-effect.description: The vector-effect CSS property suppresses specific transformation effects in SVG, thus permitting effects like a road on a map staying the same width no matter how the map is zoomed, or allowing a diagram key to retain its position and size regardless of other transforms. It can only be used with SVG elements that accept the "vector-effect" attribute. When used, the CSS value overrides any values of the element's vector-effect attribute.

vertical-align.name: vertical-align
vertical-align.description: The vertical-align CSS shorthand property sets the vertical alignment of an inline, inline-block, or table-cell box.

view-timeline.name: view-timeline
view-timeline.description: The view-timeline CSS shorthand property defines a named view progress timeline's name, direction, and inset values.

view-timeline-axis.name: view-timeline-axis
view-timeline-axis.description: The view-timeline-axis CSS property specifies the scroll direction to be used for a named view progress timeline.

view-timeline-inset.name: view-timeline-inset
view-timeline-inset.description: The view-timeline-inset CSS property is used to specify one or two values representing an adjustment to the position of the scrollport (see "Scroll container" for more details) in which the subject element of a named view progress timeline animation is deemed to be visible. Put another way, this allows you to specify start and/or end inset (or outset) values that offset the position of the timeline.

view-timeline-name.name: view-timeline-name
view-timeline-name.description: The view-timeline-name CSS property specifies the names of one or more named view progress timelines associated with the element.

view-transition-class.name: view-transition-class
view-transition-class.description: The view-transition-class CSS property provides the selected elements with one or more identifying classes ("custom-ident"s), providing an additional method of styling the view transitions for those elements.

view-transition-name.name: view-transition-name
view-transition-name.description: The view-transition-name CSS property specifies the view transition snapshot that selected elements will participate in. This enables you to animate those elements separately from the rest of the page, which uses the default cross-fade animation during a view transition. You can then define custom animation styles for these elements.

view-transition-scope.name: view-transition-scope
view-transition-scope.description: The view-transition-scope CSS property enables the discoverability of elements with "view-transition-name" values set on them (and therefore the creation of view transition snapshots) to be isolated to a specific element subtree.

visibility.name: visibility
visibility.description: The visibility CSS property shows or hides an element without changing the layout of a document. The property can also hide rows or columns in a "table".

white-space.name: white-space
white-space.description: The white-space CSS shorthand property sets how "whitespace", "white space" inside an element is handled.

white-space-collapse.name: white-space-collapse
white-space-collapse.description: The white-space-collapse CSS property controls how "whitespace", "white space" inside an element is collapsed.
white-space-collapse.syntax: collapse | discard | preserve | preserve-breaks | preserve-spaces | break-spaces

widows.name: widows
widows.description: The widows CSS property sets the minimum number of lines in a block container that must be shown at the top of a page, region, or column.
widows.appliesTo: block containers that establish an inline formatting context

width.name: width
width.description: The width CSS property sets an element's width. By default, it sets the width of the content area, but if "box-sizing" is set to border-box, it sets the width of the border area.

will-change.name: will-change
will-change.description: The will-change CSS property enables optimizing animations by providing a rendering hint to a browser about how an element is expected to change.

word-break.name: word-break
word-break.description: The word-break CSS property sets whether line breaks appear wherever the text would otherwise overflow its content box.
word-break.syntax: normal | break-all | keep-all | manual | auto-phrase | break-word

word-spacing.name: word-spacing
word-spacing.description: The word-spacing CSS property sets the spacing between words and between tags.

writing-mode.name: writing-mode
writing-mode.description: The writing-mode CSS property sets whether lines of text are laid out horizontally or vertically, as well as the direction in which text flows.
writing-mode.appliesTo: All elements except table row groups, table column groups, table rows, table columns, ruby base containers, ruby annotation containers

x.name: x
x.description: The x CSS property defines the x-axis coordinate of the top left corner of the SVG "rect" shape, "image" image, "foreignObject" viewport or nested "svg" viewport relative to the nearest ancestor's user coordinate system. If present, it overrides the element's "x" attribute.

y.name: y
y.description: The y CSS property defines the y-axis coordinate of the top left corner of the SVG "rect" shape, "image" image, "foreignObject" viewport and nested "svg" viewport relative to the nearest ancestor's user coordinate system. If present, it overrides the element's "y" attribute.

z-index.name: z-index
z-index.description: The z-index CSS property sets the z-order of a positioned element and its descendants or flex and grid items. Overlapping elements with a larger z-index cover those with a smaller one.

zoom.name: zoom
zoom.description: The zoom CSS property can be used to control the magnification level of an element. "transform-function/scale", "transform: scale()" can be used as an alternative to this property.
zoom.appliesTo: all <length> property values of all elements
